summary: The Longer Catechism, a standard Russian Orthodox statement of the faith, says that until the general resurrection the souls of the righteous are in light and rest with a foretaste of happiness, and those of the wicked are in the reverse state, with full retribution coming after the resurrection of the body and the last judgment. Souls who died in faith without time to bear fruits of repentance may be helped toward a blessed resurrection by prayers and works of mercy, especially the bloodless sacrifice of the Liturgy. Christ will come to judge in glory, and the catechism speaks of everlasting happiness and everlasting torment. The questions read do not use the word purgatory.

points.question: Is there a purification after death?
points.answer: Souls of the righteous are in light and rest and the wicked in the reverse, until the general resurrection. Prayers for souls who died in faith without bearing fruit, especially the Liturgy, may help them toward a blessed resurrection.

points.question: What is the final state of the wicked?
points.answer: The catechism speaks of everlasting torment alongside everlasting happiness, when it urges meditation on death, the resurrection, the last judgment, and each.

points.question: What happens when Christ returns?
points.answer: He will come to judge in glory with all the holy angels, and perfect retribution according to works is received after the resurrection of the body and God's last judgment.

review.note: Questions 214-215, 229, 372-376 and 385 read in the azbyka.ru English text on 2026-11-12. "No purgatory" and "everlasting punishment" are our reading: the catechism describes a rest or torment of souls until the resurrection and mentions everlasting torment, but does not discuss purgatory or hell at length in the questions read. The Orthodox Confession addresses purgatory directly. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
